_about: Research themes grounded in published asset-pricing evidence. 'cluster' follows the 13 themes of Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen (2023) where applicable. Seeds are starting points, not submissions: every seed is checked by the validator in tests, but none has been simulated by this repo.

themes.name: Short-term reversal
themes.hypothesis: Last week's losers outperform last week's winners as liquidity-driven price pressure reverts.
themes.mechanism: Liquidity providers demand compensation for absorbing order imbalances; the reversal is stronger within industry, where common news is netted out.
cautions: High turnover by construction: start at Decay 4 and climb the decay ladder.
Very crowded on BRAIN; expect self-correlation against other reversal alphas.

themes.name: Intermediate-horizon momentum (12-1)
themes.hypothesis: Stocks with high returns over the past year, skipping the most recent month, keep outperforming.
themes.mechanism: Under-reaction to firm-specific news and gradual information diffusion; the skipped month avoids the short-term reversal.
cautions: Momentum crashes after market rebounds; regime gating (calm_regime_gate) can help.
Industry momentum and stock momentum differ: neutralization choice matters.

themes.name: Gross profitability
themes.hypothesis: Firms with high gross profits relative to assets earn higher future returns.
themes.mechanism: Gross profit is the cleanest measure of economic productivity, less distorted by accounting choices further down the income statement.
cautions: Write (revenue - cogs) / assets with parentheses: revenue - cogs / assets divides only cogs.
Low turnover: watch the 1% minimum and do not add decay.

themes.name: Return on equity / operating profitability
themes.hypothesis: More profitable firms (high operating income per unit of book equity) have higher expected returns.
themes.mechanism: In the investment-based q-factor model, expected returns rise with expected profitability for a given investment level.
cautions: Negative book equity makes the ratio meaningless: consider operating_income / assets as a robustness check.

themes.name: Asset growth / investment
themes.hypothesis: Firms that grow their asset base aggressively subsequently underperform.
themes.mechanism: Firms invest more when their cost of capital is low (investment CAPM), and investors extrapolate past growth.
cautions: Year-over-year changes in quarterly data are lumpy: ts_backfill before ts_delay if coverage is patchy.

themes.name: Value
themes.hypothesis: Cheap stocks (high fundamentals relative to price) outperform expensive ones.
themes.mechanism: Risk compensation for distressed firms and/or over-extrapolation of growth for expensive firms.
cautions: Valuation ratios differ structurally across industries: always compare within industry.
Value has had long drawdowns; pair with quality to avoid value traps.

themes.name: Accruals
themes.hypothesis: Earnings backed by accruals rather than cash flow are less persistent; high-accrual firms underperform.
themes.mechanism: Investors fixate on reported earnings and under-weight the lower persistence of the accrual component.
cautions: Cash flow and income may update on different dates; ts_backfill both if coverage is uneven.

themes.name: Short-term liquidity / balance-sheet safety
themes.hypothesis: Firms that can cover short-term debt with liquid assets are safer and outperform peers that cannot.
themes.mechanism: Financial distress risk is mispriced; investors underreact to weak short-term solvency.
seeds: group_rank(operating_income / assets, subindustry) - group_rank(cash_st / debt_st, subindustry)
group_rank(operating_income / assets, subindustry) - group_rank(cash_st / (cash_st + debt_st), subindustry)
cautions: Observed on BRAIN (USA TOP3000 D1, subindustry): group_zscore(cash_st / debt_st, subindustry) Sharpe -0.79 and group_rank(ts_backfill(cash_st, 63) / ts_backfill(debt_st, 63), subindustry) Sharpe -0.83. The raw liquidity ratio has the opposite sign to the hypothesis: cash-rich firms with little short-term debt are often unprofitable growth firms, while mature profitable firms run lean on cash. The seeds pair the flipped ratio with profitability.
Firms with near-zero short-term debt produce extreme ratios; cash_st / (cash_st + debt_st) stays in [0, 1].

themes.name: Quality (profitable, safe, low leverage)
themes.hypothesis: High-quality firms (profitable, stable, conservatively financed) earn higher risk-adjusted returns.
themes.mechanism: Investors overpay for speculative 'junk' and underpay for boring quality.
seeds: group_rank(operating_income / assets, sector) + group_rank(-debt / assets, sector)
cautions: Composite scores correlate with plain profitability alphas; check structural similarity first.

themes.name: Debt issuance
themes.hypothesis: Firms that raise new debt subsequently underperform firms that pay it down.
themes.mechanism: Managers issue when financing is cheap or the firm is overvalued; analysts are over-optimistic about issuers.
cautions: Utilities and financials use leverage structurally: industry comparison is essential.

themes.name: Low risk (volatility / beta)
themes.hypothesis: Low-volatility stocks earn higher risk-adjusted returns than high-volatility stocks.
themes.mechanism: Leverage-constrained investors bid up high-risk stocks (Frazzini & Pedersen 2014). Novy-Marx & Velikov (2022) show the BAB result depends on micro-cap-heavy weighting and costs, so implement it only in liquid universes with heavy smoothing.
cautions: Avoid TOP3000 tails: the anomaly concentrates in illiquid names.
Second seed shorts high-volatility firms with deteriorating cash flows (a 'bad beta' tilt), not volatility alone.

themes.name: Return seasonality
themes.hypothesis: Stocks tend to earn similar returns in the same calendar month across years.
themes.mechanism: Recurring flows and information events (earnings timing, fiscal-year effects) repeat annually.
cautions: ts_delay(ts_sum(returns, 21), 231) is the return over the same upcoming month one year ago.

themes.name: High-volume return premium
themes.hypothesis: Stocks with unusually high recent trading volume subsequently outperform.
themes.mechanism: Volume shocks raise visibility and investor attention, increasing demand.
cautions: Volume ratios spike around earnings; combine with trade_when gating to make it event-driven.

themes.name: Customer-supplier momentum
themes.hypothesis: Returns of a firm's major customers predict the firm's own returns because the news reaches suppliers with a lag.
themes.mechanism: Limited investor attention: information about linked firms diffuses slowly.
cautions: Needs a relationship/supply-chain dataset; find the grouping or vector fields on the BRAIN Data page and add them to the field dictionary first.
Relationship vector fields must be collapsed with vec_avg/vec_sum before any matrix operator.

themes.name: Post-earnings announcement drift / analyst revisions
themes.hypothesis: Prices under-react to earnings surprises and analyst revisions, drifting in the direction of the news for weeks.
themes.mechanism: Investors under-weight the persistence of earnings news.
cautions: Needs analyst-estimate fields; confirm IDs on the BRAIN Data page.
Event gating with trade_when makes this naturally low-correlation.

themes.name: Size
themes.hypothesis: Smaller firms earn higher returns than larger firms, mainly once junk is controlled for.
cautions: The raw size effect is weak in liquid universes; use it as a tilt inside other ideas rather than alone.
